newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian Total profit drop confirms fears.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian Total profit drop confirms fears.

text.p: A drop in half-year profits at Nigeria's Total oil marketing company on Monday has confirmed the fears of analysts that the sector is set for a series a poor results.
After-tax profits fell by 19 percent to 504 million naira to end-June 1996 from 620 million naira in 1995.
"The continued stagnation in fuel margins and difficulties deriving from the unavailability of products generally were the main causes for the relative decline," a company spokesman said.
Share traders said last week the oil marketers were holding back their results because they feared share prices would fall due to the expected lower results.
Oil marketing companies have made consistent gains on the stock exchange.
Total's shares, the highest priced on the exchange, closed unchanged at 49.05 naira on Monday.
"Any loss of confidence is likely to be only temporary, as the oil companies are still going to outperform other sectors bearing in mind the recession," one trader said.
Turnover fell 20 percent to 6,426 million naira in the first six months of 1996 from 8,009 million in a similar 1995 period.
Gross profit was 697 million naira compared to 984 million in the corresponding period, down 29 percent.
An estimated 193 million naira was provided for taxation against 364 million in the same period.
